native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: SES (socioeconomic status) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion falls from 0.3636 to -0.2293 and loses significance once race and academic characteristics are jointly included. In our data (logistic regression, raw units, N=8773, 236 BA completions) SES is +0.3524 (OR 1.42, p=6.1e-5) with race only, and -0.2316 (OR 0.79, p=0.021; Firth -0.2294) once the ASVAB composite and class percentile are added - the only predictor whose sign flips. Mechanism: SES proxies academic resources (corr with ASVAB 0.463, with class percentile 0.304); once those are controlled, SES adds no advantage for BA completion (average marginal effect on probability moves from +0.0092 to -0.0057 at a 2.69% base rate), i.e. the SES-BA link is mediated by unequal academic resources rather than SES itself. Race likewise loses significance after academic controls (Black vs White +0.093, p=0.68). Observational mediation, not a causal claim (no survey weights, mediator measured once).
